driverRegime.method: daily % change of each asset regressed on the daily change in the US 2-year and 10-year yields (basis points) and on the daily % change in WTI; a driver is dominant when |corr| >= 0.4

dataNotes: Run timing: this cycle ran the morning of 6 October 2026 after the GitHub Actions pre-open fetch job drafted contracts/*.2026-10-05.json from Monday 5 October's close. Every figure is dated at or before the 2026-10-05 close; news-log entries dated 6 October (futures up, oil slide, Option Care deal) were deliberately not used.

Bonds, dollar and IWM sigma are not auto-fetched and were carried stale: bonds 15 (TLT 30-day implied volatility, 25 September), dollar 4.72 (EUR/USD 1-month implied volatility, 21 September), IWM 19.97 (RVX, 23 September). No newer prints were obtainable.

Source notes: the news log has the S&P 500 cash index at 7,775.30 (+0.68%) and the 10-year yield at 5.35% (+7bp) on 5 October, while the 10-year note future ZN=F fell only 0.13%; the drafted ES=F/NQ=F/RTY=F/GC=F/DX-Y.NYB closes are used for all numbers. The log's 5 October payrolls entry cites a roughly +150K consensus, whereas the 2 October entry cites about +84K to +90K; no vote depends on the consensus figure.

No 5 October high-yield OAS, MOVE, breadth counts, positioning print or seasonal statistic was obtainable, and the 5 October ISM/S&P Global services PMI results were not found; credit, breadth, positioning, volatility, calendar and seasonality votes are neutral. AAII (32.7/19.2/48.1) is the week to 23 September, the newest obtainable.

Fed odds: the October hike probability of about 16% (from 64% a week earlier) is the 2 October news-log figure; the 5 October entry confirms reduced hike bets without a new number. FOMC minutes are due Wednesday 7 October per the log.

News-log entries for 2026-10-05 (euro low/French spreads, futures slip, oil split, payrolls/10-year high, index close, Houthi/Hormuz, TSMC/SpaceX) were already in data/news_log.json; the Artifact database returned the same entries for 2 to 6 October, so no merge was needed. No hand-entered issue entries were dated 5 October.

newsLog.event: Euro hits a 17-month low as French political gridlock stokes budget-deficit fears; French-German bond spread widens to its highest since 2011; US 10Y yield edges higher
newsLog.numbers: 10Y 5.31% (+0.03); French-German spread widest since 2011; euro at 17-month low
newsLog.tickers: TLT, 10Y, yield, Treasury, DXY, USD, dollar, SPY
newsLog.reaction: Rising yields and euro weakness (firmer dollar) weighed on equity futures into the open

newsLog.event: US stock futures edge lower as bond yields stay near 20-year highs; light data/earnings calendar, S&P Global and ISM PMIs due; Fed minutes later in week; Nasdaq still near record highs
newsLog.tickers: SPY, S&P, QQQ, Nasdaq, IWM, Russell, GLD, gold
newsLog.reaction: Muted, slightly lower open indicated; small caps modestly firmer, gold bid

newsLog.event: Oil mixed: Brent holds above $100 and Murban near $110 on Hormuz/Red Sea risk premium, tanker shortages and high freight, while US WTI edges lower
newsLog.reaction: Seaborne crude carries a wider geopolitical premium than US crude; energy names supported

newsLog.event: September payrolls rose just 29,000, far below expectations, as unemployment climbed to 4.2%; reduced odds of another Fed rate hike in October, while long-end Treasury yields extended to fresh multi-decade highs ahead of Wednesday's FOMC minutes
newsLog.reaction: Equities shrugged off bond-market caution as softer jobs data cooled Fed hike bets even as yields pushed higher on term-premium/supply concerns

newsLog.event: US stocks closed higher, led by tech, as investors looked past rising bond yields; Nasdaq notched a fresh high on strength in TSMC and SpaceX-linked names
newsLog.reaction: Tech-led gains outweighed bond-market jitters; Dow lagged as rate-sensitive sectors underperformed

newsLog.event: Houthis claimed missile/drone strikes on Saudi Aramco facilities in Riyadh and Khurais (Sat Oct 3); Iran's parliament speaker said the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until Washington meets seven conditions (Sun Oct 4); G7 weighing an emergency release of ~100 million barrels of crude/diesel
newsLog.numbers: Brent $102.30/bbl; WTI $90.62/bbl (-0.5%); Brent-WTI spread >$11 (vs normal $3-5); Murban ~$110/bbl
newsLog.reaction: Seaborne Middle East crude (Brent/Murban) carries a wider war-risk premium than US crude even as Brent eased on rising regional exports and reported G7 release plans

newsLog.event: TSMC shares hit an intraday all-time high after Elon Musk confirmed early-stage talks for TSMC to join his 'Terafab' chip-fab project supplying Tesla, SpaceX and xAI; Intel (an existing Terafab partner) fell on the news. Separately, SpaceX (SPCX) jumped after Morgan Stanley's Adam Jonas reiterated Overweight with a $300 price target
newsLog.numbers: TSM +2.79% (record high); INTC approx -2%; SPCX +7.63% to $171.09 (MS $300 PT, ~89% implied upside)
newsLog.reaction: AI/chip-supply optimism lifted semis and SpaceX; Jonas called SPCX shares 'cheap and getting cheaper' versus AI mega-cap peers
